item.title: France's Mélenchon to stage major campaign rally for manifesto launch
item.description: The leader of the hard-left France Unbowed party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, is currently polling second ahead of next spring's presidential elections, according to a poll conducted in late October.

item.title: Switzerland: Giant banner targets Big Tech outside data centre site
item.description: Greenpeace activists unfurled a giant 26-by-26-metre banner outside a data centre construction site in Beringen, northeastern Switzerland, on Friday 6 November, protesting against the growing environmental impact of major technology companies.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 6th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Elon Musk's Tesla to 'wind down' Cybertruck production next year
item.description: Musk said the decision was taken in order to make room for increased production of its Cybercab robotaxi. The move comes after years of weaker-than-expected sales for the futuristic electric pickup.

item.title: Spain: Vintage cars hit the streets of Almería for annual rally
item.description: Around 40 vintage and classic cars have taken to the streets of Almería for the 36th edition of an annual rally. From a rare 1905 Vermorel to a DeLorean, the event celebrates more than a century of motoring history.

item.title: ‘We vote with our money’: What are the biggest commercial opportunities of EU enlargement?
item.description: “The European market is the best market in the world,” says investment expert Jan Růžička, urging policymakers to accelerate EU accession and the Capital Markets Union to maintain momentum and sustain enthusiasm among candidate countries.

item.title: Meghan Markle's father reportedly arrested in Florida over alleged child porn possession
item.description: Markle Sr's arrest follows an investigation launched after his son, Thomas Markle Jr, reportedly discovered boxes containing hundreds or potentially thousands of images at his father's former home in the Philippines.

item.title: Iran delivers secret Khamenei message to Putin as Moscow pushes gas pipeline deal
item.description: Iran’s Security Council chief, Mohsen Rezaei, went to Moscow to deliver a personal message from Ayatollah Khamenei and discuss building a pipeline to import Russian gas.

item.title: Singapore Airlines to invest €1.4 billion upgrading luxury long-haul cabins
item.description: Updates include the largest double bed in commercial aviation in first class, pyjamas for business class passengers and Bluetooth pairing with the in-flight entertainment system.

item.title: Baku real estate expo showcases Azerbaijan’s tech-driven urban future
item.description: What makes a city attractive to investors and the people who live there? From affordable housing and urban planning to smart technologies and changing lifestyles, Azerbaijan’s first International Real Estate Exhibition put the future of the built environment in focus.

item.title: Tiny Spanish island quits coal for good amid renewables boom — but country struggling to electrify
item.description: Authorisation has been granted to permanently close down the remaining coal-fired units on Majorca, marking a new era for the island.

item.title: Group of lawyers suing French interior minister over protesters' life-changing injuries
item.description: Lawyers representing at least 18 people injured during recent demonstrations in France say they will take legal acton against Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez.

item.title: From street eats to Michelin stars: Why foodies should visit Macao in 2027
item.description: It’s a big year for Macao in 2027 as it celebrates 10 years of being a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy. Travellers are invited to explore its fusion food scene as well as its ‘quieter’ spots.

item.title: Kazakhstan’s growth to pick up in 2027 despite geopolitical tensions, IMF says
item.description: The IMF expects Kazakhstan’s economy to grow by 4.9% in 2027, up from 4.4% this year. Kazakhstan is forecast to grow faster than any other oil exporter in the IMF’s Middle East and Central Asia group in 2026.

item.title: Data centre backlash: Which AI companies have been affected by US midterm results?
item.description: OpenAI has gone on a charm offensive, while semiconductor companies worldwide have seen their stocks plunge.

item.title: Uzbekistan announces record cotton harvest as President Mirziyoyev sets higher 2027 yield target
item.description: Officials say Uzbekistan harvested more than five million tonnes of raw cotton, about 25% more than in 2025, with machines picking around 85% of the crop.

item.title: Belgian king refuses PM Bart De Wever's resignation and asks him to restart budget talks
item.description: De Wever, a Flemish conservative, handed in his resignation on Monday amid a continuing budget crisis that has seen coalition partners fail to agree on a 2027 spending plan.

item.title: Netherlands: Protesters storm Amsterdam data centre construction site
item.description: Protesters broke into a data centre construction site intended for Microsoft in Amsterdam, on 6 November, climbing cranes and unfurling banners denouncing artificial intelligence and the company's alleged involvement in the war in Gaza.

item.title: Baku's 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue examines the role of culture in peace
item.description: The 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue in Baku brought together cultural figures, religious leaders and international representatives to explore how art, faith and dialogue can bridge divisions, challenge prejudice and promote peace and mutual understanding.

item.title: Spain, Italy, Greece and Cyprus to benefit from EU asylum solidarity scheme in 2027
item.description: The European Commission has identified four Mediterranean countries as facing migratory pressure, opening the door to asylum seeker relocations. The Ceuta crisis will have little impact on numbers, while Hungary and Slovakia have failed to contribute to EU solidarity efforts.

item.title: Scientists develop first-ever “broad-spectrum” bird flu vaccine using AI
item.description: Scientists used AI to design a vaccine capable of protecting against a wide range of bird flu variants. That’s a game changer for national biosecurity and more resilient public health systems, they say.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Ukraine forge new energy defence and trade agreements
item.description: An Azerbaijani delegation led by its energy minister travelled to Ukraine to sign a 2026-2027 Action Plan. Bilateral talks focused on emergency winter grid equipment, joint manufacturing, and expanding European transit via the Trans-Balkan route.

item.title: EU tells TikTok to change 'harmful' For You feed over 'rabbit hole effect'
item.description: Brussels says TikTok's recommendation algorithm risks exposing children and vulnerable users to harmful content. The platform has rejected the findings as "fundamentally inaccurate".

item.title: Why Spain is taking 188,000 tonnes of olive oil off the market
item.description: The world’s biggest olive oil producer is holding back 12% of its output from November to stop producer prices falling further. It’s the first time Spain has used the measure, which is expected to keep about 188,000 tonnes off the market until the end of September 2027.

item.title: UK: Thousands gather as London switches on its Christmas lights
item.description: Thousands of people gathered on London's Regent Street on Thursday 5 November as the famous shopping destination welcomed the Christmas season with a spectacular lights switch-on and fireworks display.

item.title: Could Thailand be your second home? Inside the membership that helps you stay for years
item.description: The Thailand Privilege Card offers long-stay visa options through memberships lasting up to 20 years, with perks ranging from priority airport services and luxury experiences to practical help with setting up a new life in the country.

item.title: Scotland wants visitors to stay longer, slow down and experience authentic hospitality
item.description: From sheep shearing and Highland ‘coo’ encounters to the Tour de France and a new World Rally Championship event, Scotland has plenty in store for the year ahead.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV departs for Uruguay as he begins tour of South America
item.description: Leo is scheduled to head on to Argentina, where he is due to visit Buenos Aires, Córdoba and Luján. In Peru, the pontiff is also scheduled to appear in Chiclayo, Cusco, and Pucallpa.

item.title: Cycling, castles and outdoor adventures: Wales gears up for a busy 2027
item.description: The Tour de France, a year-long celebration of cycling and Wrexham’s growing Hollywood profile are among the attractions putting Wales in the spotlight.

item.title: Who is Ilija Srdanović? The doctor who took Serbia’s student movement to Macron and EU leaders
item.description: Cardiologist Ilija Srdanović has become the international face of Serbia’s Student List, fielding calls from Macron, Costa and Plenković. But it is still unclear whether he will emerge as the leader of the future Serbian government.

item.title: German carmakers drive surprise rise in industrial output
item.description: Industrial output in Europe’s largest economy rose 0.7% in September from the previous month, beating expectations. Car production led the gains, helped by a rebound in pharmaceuticals, while construction output fell.

item.title: Trio suspected of attempting to smuggle 3,000 tarantulas into Germany
item.description: In November 2023, Interpol said the black market for illegal wildlife products was worth up to $20 billion a year.

item.title: How Greece aims to become a year-round destination as it looks beyond its beaches and islands
item.description: From mountain escapes and wine trails to wellness retreats and city breaks, the country is hoping to draw visitors beyond the traditional summer season, Greece’s tourism minister tells Euronews Travel.

item.title: Five people rescued off Kiribati after months drifting at sea
item.description: In a statement shared on Sunday, the governor of Micronesia's Chuuk state, Alexander Narruhn, said he was in talks with the Kiribati government to bring the survivors home.

item.title: Parents sue Google after 13-year-old allegedly used AI to plan suicide
item.description: The case raises further concerns about AI safety for children as tech companies face more lawsuits over their technology.

item.title: Big Tech and green groups meet to discuss the future of data centres in the US
item.description: As artificial intelligence drives demand for more data centres, some of the world's biggest technology companies are joining forces with environmental groups to address concerns over their impact on local communities in the United States.

item.title: EU prosecutors probe fraud claims over funds for Spanish rail line hit by deadly crash
item.description: EU prosecutors have opened a fraud investigation into funds for upgrading Spain’s Madrid–Seville high-speed line, where a 28 October crash near Urda killed 69. A similar probe began in March after a January crash on the same line killed 46.

item.title: Japan: Commuters flock to see two goats grazing at Tokyo station
item.description: Two white goats have become unlikely celebrities in central Tokyo after being recruited to clear overgrown vegetation near Yotsuya railway station. Their eco-friendly gardening duties are attracting crowds of delighted onlookers.

item.title: Hormuz standoff ‘not sustainable’, senior Iranian lawmaker tells Euronews
item.description: MP and foreign minister under Ahmadinejad, Manouchehr Mottaki, told Euronews that multiple ships a day were being disabled as the IRGC Navy worked to bring unauthorised transit to zero. He called on Washington to lift its naval blockade strangling the Iranian economy before talks resume.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 6th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU and UK set to link carbon markets in major post-Brexit deal
item.description: The agreement to link EU and UK carbon markets, expected to be announced at the 20 November summit, could spare manufacturers additional carbon border charges, but critics warn that closer alignment could drive up costs for British industry.

item.title: Irish media outlets evacuate staff in Dublin following bomb threats
item.description: It comes amid a flurry of bomb hoaxes targeting European airlines and around a week before Dublin is due to host a meeting of the European Political Community.

item.title: Bomb threats continue to target aircrafts across Europe
item.description: The latest incidents follow a wave of bomb scares that affected at least 25 flights across Europe on Thursday.

item.title: Emergency services deployed after school bus crash kills two in France
item.description: A minor and a young adult were killed when a bus carrying pupils crashed in eastern France on Friday morning. Emergency services deployed helicopters to the scene as authorities launched an investigation into the circumstances.

item.title: Exclusive: US is 'playing politics' with Patriot missiles - Finnish minister
item.description: Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen tells Euronews that European allies have already paid for the Patriot interceptor missiles, but Washington has yet to approve their delivery as Ukraine braces for further Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure.

item.title: 'An insult to his culture': Italian chef loses job after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
item.description: Chef Davide Tamburella refused to put the tropical fruit on pizzas at a restaurant in Brisbane, Australia, calling it "an insult to his culture". Having been fired from his job, he has lost his legal battle against the establishment.

item.title: Inside the EU’s battle to bar Russian war veterans from Europe
item.description: Ukraine has shared the names of more than half a million Russian soldiers, but fewer than 1% have been added to the EU’s Schengen security database. Brussels is now exploring ways to overcome the legal hurdles amid growing concerns over Russian security threats.

item.title: Europe's climate tax risks opening a new trade war with India at COP31
item.description: The EU's diplomatic stance at COP31 summit is complicated by its own political retreat on climate policy and growing global opposition to its carbon border tax.

item.title: Poland warns allies: Don't negotiate with Russia over Eastern Europe's head
item.description: Poland has warned that Eastern Europe's security interests must not be sidelined in negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, as it pushes back against efforts to resume Russian gas imports.

item.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's massive 'triumphal arch'
item.description: Trump has said the structure would be turned into a "top grade military complex" housing drones, snipers and ammunition.
